generic_ballot.source_label: Polling Forecast-compatible merged poll feed plus verified primary-source additions
generic_ballot.display_type: polling average, not an election-day forecast

external_poll.status: public context only; not included in the district forecast

latest_polls.sample_note: n=2,000; reported average expected error ±2.2 pp (pollwide, not an interval for the D-R difference).
Likely-voter n=1,000; reported credibility interval ±3 pp (not an interval for the D-R difference).

generic_ballot.margin_definition: D/R two-party margin: 100 × (D share − R share) / (D share + R share).
generic_ballot.timing_rule: Fieldwork ends by 2026-11-01; verified first-public dates after the cutoff are excluded, while unknown timing remains unknown and is retained under the established rule. The Polling Forecast API snapshot is as of 2026-10-31. The Big Data Poll release date was verified as 2026-10-31 from the pollster page.
generic_ballot.source_coverage_note: The latest API snapshot does not include first-public dates for most records; fieldwork dates are not used as a substitute. The new Big Data Poll has a verified October 31 first-public date.

House.method: The 435 district probabilities are combined with an independent-race Poisson-binomial PMF. For the selected >35 percentage-point disagreement rule, the companion seat forecast's current-input probabilities are used for the affected races. A common shift to Toss-up, Leans, and Likely margins then makes the number of Democratic district favorites match the companion forecast's hard-call total; Safe probabilities are unchanged. Expected seats, district favorites, and the seat-distribution median are separate quantities. Single-party candidate display adjustments do not change the PMF.

Senate.coverage_note: 35 forecast races plus 65 fixed seats (34 Democratic-caucus, 31 Republican).

Governor.coverage_note: Covers 36 Governor races; source coverage is documented in the private release audit.

senate_seat_distribution.interpretation: Approximate range across the 35 listed Senate races and 65 seats already held; not a party-control probability.

summary.seat_range_note: Seat ranges summarize the published race forecasts and are best read alongside their expected totals.

governor_seat_distribution.interpretation: Range of Democratic wins among the 36 Governor races; not a party-control probability.

generic_ballot_forecast.target: National Democratic-minus-Republican House two-party popular-vote margin in percentage points

historical_performance.validation_explanation: House validation uses the established 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024 covered-race cohorts. The selected >35 percentage-point disagreement rule is applied before validation; one common shift to non-Safe margins in each election makes the number of Democratic district favorites match the companion seat forecast's hard-call total. Probabilities are recalculated from those margins using the saved historical calibration. Expected seats and the seat-distribution median may differ from the hard-call target. The pooled mean annual absolute hard-seat error is the mean of the four per-election absolute errors. These are retrospective results from four related election environments, not independent future tests.
historical_performance.governor_calibration_explanation: Governor win probabilities use a proprietary probability calibration. The 2018-2024 cycles informed selection for both incumbent and challenger; the paired scorecard is validation evidence, not an independent holdout.

forecast_release_note: November 1 House update: the selected >35 percentage-point disagreement rule applies the companion seat forecast's current-input probabilities to affected races. A shared non-Safe margin shift matches its 210 Democratic hard calls. The House expected total is 211.418; the displayed favorite count is 210 and the seat-distribution median is 211. The November 1 generic, Senate, and Governor streams remain unchanged.
